scenes.headline: How a 45M model runs on a $5 chip
scenes.sub: MimiModel: weights read in place from flash, and 20 points in the decode loop.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Guava! MimiModel runs a forty-five million parameter tool-calling model on a five dollar microcontroller. Here's how it fits.

scenes.label: The trick
scenes.text: Move the Hadamard transform off the weights and onto the activation, and the 2-bit weights never have to leave flash.
scenes.say: The trick: rebuilding each weight needs a Hadamard transform. Apply it to the activation instead, and the packed weights never leave flash.

scenes.title: The identity that keeps weights in flash
scenes.say: Each group of a hundred twenty-eight weights is stored as two-bit indices and a norm, and rebuilding it multiplies by a Hadamard matrix, H.

parts.note: rebuild every weight group: 13.7 MB, every token
parts.say: On the weights, that's thirteen point seven megabytes expanded every token, with five hundred twelve kilobytes of RAM.

parts.note: transform the activation once, shared by every output row
parts.say: But H is symmetric and orthogonal, so it moves onto the activation: computed once, and shared by every output row.

steps.say: So the packed two-bit bytes stay memory-mapped in flash, read in place by the dot product. The activation sits in fast internal scratch.
PSRAM holds the KV cache. Nothing is ever loaded, so startup takes forty-eight milliseconds.

scenes.title: Same weights, three decode-loop fixes
scenes.say: With byte-identical weights, the engine first scored forty-eight point eight percent against the official sixty-nine point two. The gap was in the decode loop.

items.say: Reason up to two hundred fifty-six tokens, not ninety, before forcing JSON: forty-four rows.
Keep the system prompt as an attention sink instead of evicting it: sixty-three rows.
Check every byte against one grammar instead of forcing JSON in pieces: ninety-six rows. Together, sixty-nine point six percent.

scenes.text: Twenty points lived in the decode loop, not the weights. Check your harness before you blame the model.
scenes.say: Twenty points lived in the decode loop, not the weights. Check your harness before blaming the model.

recap: The Hadamard transform moves onto the activation
2-bit weights are read in place from flash
Three decode-loop fixes, same weights, 20 points
scenes.say: To recap: transform the activation, leave weights in flash, and find lost points in the decode loop.
